title: A Fibre-Integrated SPDC Heralded Single-Photon Source Using Zn-Indiffused PPLN Ridge Waveguides at Telecom Wavelengths
authors: Peter Iveson, Paolo L. Mennea, Goronwy Tawy, Rex H. S. Bannerman, Noe Palomar-Davidson, Lewis D. Wright, Patrick M. Ledingham, Peter G. R. Smith, James C. Gates, Corin B. E. Gawith
abstract: We report a fibre-integrated heralded single-photon source based on a commercial Zn-indiffused MgO:PPLN ridge waveguide operated in Type-0 degenerate spontaneous parametric down-conversion (SPDC). The device emits a broadband spectrum spanning approximately 70 nm across the telecom C-and L-bands, with an absolute brightness of $9.1\times 10^{9}$ pairs/(s mW). After accounting for optical losses, we determine an internal heralding efficiency of 58(5)%. The source maintains high purity, exhibiting a coincidences-to-accidentals ratio exceeding $9\times 10^{4}$ and a heralded second-order correlation of $g_{\text{h}}^{(2)}(0) = (5.53 \pm 0.46)\times 10^{-4}$. Low multi-photon noise and broadband emission demonstrate the viability of such platforms for wavelength-multiplexed quantum networking.
summary: The authors report on a high-performance, fibre-integrated single-photon source utilizing Zn-indiffused PPLN waveguides pumped via degenerate SPDC. The system demonstrates excellent purity and brightness across telecom wavelengths, establishing it as a robust platform for wavelength-multiplexed quantum networking applications.
main_problem: To characterize a fibre-integrated heralded single-photon source based on spontaneous parametric down-conversion (SPDC) using Zn-indiffused PPLN ridge waveguides at telecom wavelengths.
main_result: The source achieved high performance metrics, including an absolute brightness of $9.1	imes 10^{9}$ pairs/(s mW), a low heralded second-order correlation ($g_{	ext{h}}^{(2)}(0) \approx 5.53	imes 10^{-4}$), and a competitive internal heralding efficiency of $(58 \pm 5)\%$.
method: The characterization involved measuring the broadband spectrum, quantifying pair correlations using the coincidences-to-accidentals ratio (CAR), and calculating the heralded second-order correlation function.
model_or_system: The physical system is a fibre-pigtailed MgO:PPLN ridge waveguide module operating in Type-0 degenerate SPDC. The analysis utilized numerical modeling via a fully vectorial optical mode solver (FIMMWAVE) to predict theoretical pair generation rates and modal profiles.
key_observables: Absolute brightness ($9.1	imes 10^{9}$ pairs/(s mW)), internal heralding efficiency ($(58 \pm 5)\%$), coincidences-to-accidentals ratio ($> 9	imes 10^4$), and heralded second-order correlation ($g_{	ext{h}}^{(2)}(0) = (5.53 \pm 0.46)	imes 10^{-4}$).
important_parameters: Broadband emission spanning $\approx 70 	ext{ nm}$ across the C- and L-bands; theoretical pair generation rate ($	ext{R}_{	ext{SPDC}}/	ext{P}$) $\approx 2.7 	imes 10^{10}$ pairs $	ext{s}^{-1} 	ext{mW}^{-1}$.
main_assumptions: The reported performance metrics are based on a comprehensive characterization that accounts for optical losses and the specific waveguide structure.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the fibre-pigtailed module, schematic of the Zn-indiffused ridge waveguide, mode analysis showing index contrast profiles at different wavelengths, and experimental setups for SPDC generation and bandwidth measurement.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first reporting initial source performance metrics, followed by detailed characterization of the waveguide structure and mode modeling (including SHG measurements), culminating in the description of the full experimental SPDC measurement process to validate theoretical limits.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses quantum networking hardware by demonstrating a highly efficient, broadband, integrated photonics source, which is crucial for scalable quantum communication protocols.
